title: Fortnightly cetuximab + modified FOLFOX-6

agents.name: Cetuximab
agents.mechanism: Blocks growth messages at the cell surface
agents.explanation: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks some growth messages. In this bowel-cancer plan, validated extended RAS testing helps identify whether treatment is suitable. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care.
agents.watch: Report rash or sore nails early. Tell the nurse immediately about infusion symptoms. Eye pain, new breathing problems or severe diarrhoea need prompt advice. Blood tests check minerals during treatment and for two months afterwards.
risks: Rash, dry skin, cracks and sore nails
Infusion reaction; rare serious lung or skin effects

agents.name: Oxaliplatin
agents.explanation: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Cold can trigger tingling or throat discomfort. Tell the team about persistent numbness, difficulty with buttons or walking, or infusion symptoms. New breathing difficulty always needs assessment.
risks: Persistent sensory neuropathy, sometimes lasting after treatment
Rare serious lung or blood complications

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself.
agents.watch: The combined treatment can increase mouth soreness and diarrhoea. Report these promptly. Rare allergic reactions can occur.

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
agents.watch: Diarrhoea, mouth sores and skin soreness may become serious. Chest pain during the pump infusion needs emergency assessment. Unexpected severe early toxicity can occur even after DPD testing.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity

questions.a: This combination is used for RAS wild-type bowel cancer that has spread. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates to understand the cycle?
questions.a: No. The graph explains a general pattern. Your hospital arranges appointments; the guide and its safety information are available without entering anything.

questions.q: Will I have a pump at home?
questions.a: Confirm port/PICC preparation, pump connection, home care and professional disconnection around Day 3.

questions.q: What happens if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team checks the cause and may delay, reduce, change or stop one medicine. Ask which component changes and when you should next attend; do not restart yourself.

questions.q: How will I know whether it is helping?
questions.a: Scans, symptoms and clinical review assess benefit. A rash, side effect or good day alone cannot show whether the cancer is responding.
This NCCP regimen does not contain a routine radiotherapy course. If radiation is recommended separately, ask whether it is before, during or after these medicines.

questions.q: What about fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding?
questions.a: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. Ask for the contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine; the whole regimen may require longer precautions than one medicine alone.
RAS testing selects cetuximab treatment in colorectal cancer. It is not the selection test for the separate head-and-neck radiotherapy indication. Confirm the cancer-specific plan with your team.

phases_note: A repeating reference cycle sits within a longer treatment plan. The oncology team chooses the number of cycles and confirms changes; no patient dates are required here.
timeline_note: NCCP defines the treatment days. Symptom bands are broad educational guidance; reactions can occur on any day, and cumulative effects may continue between cycles.
safety_note: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell require immediate contact. Serious symptoms override any timeline or diary.
teachback: Can you explain which visits are planned, whether a pump is involved, and which symptoms mean you should call today? No dates or symptom scores are needed to use this guide.
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, serious and lasting risks, fertility/pregnancy precautions and the contact plan. Confirm RAS selection for colorectal treatment, infusion premedication, skin care and post-treatment mineral checks. Explain DPD testing and the exact pump schedule.
urgent_extra: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly. Call for line pain, swelling, leakage or unexpected pump progress.

chapters.title: Your treatment aim
chapters.intro: The setting changes what benefit means.

items.title: Why this option?
items.text: This combination is used for RAS wild-type bowel cancer that has spread. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

items.title: A plan that can change
items.text: This regimen is used to control advanced bowel cancer and symptoms. Ask how benefit will be assessed and whether any local treatment is part of your individual plan. Your preferences and priorities matter.

items.title: Blood tests and medicines
items.text: Review blood counts, kidney/liver tests, symptoms, allergies and all medicines and supplements. Confirm DPD testing before fluorouracil. Kidney impairment can affect uracil-based DPD testing interpretation. Tell the team about red-meat allergy or tick bites before cetuximab because these can be associated with infusion-reaction risk.

items.title: Preparing access
items.text: Confirm port/PICC preparation, pump connection, home care and professional disconnection around Day 3.

chapters.title: Symptoms in context
chapters.intro: Report what changed and how it affects you.

items.title: When to call
items.text: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly. Call for line pain, swelling, leakage or unexpected pump progress.

items.title: Bowel symptoms
items.text: Follow your written rescue plan. Fever, blood, severe pain, reduced urine or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

items.title: Skin or nerve changes
items.text: Start the prescribed skin-care plan early, use moisturiser and sun protection, and report painful or infected skin or nails. Keep mineral blood-test appointments during treatment and for two months after cetuximab.

items.title: Food, activity and practical help
items.text: Avoid cold drinks and cold exposure as instructed after oxaliplatin; do not suck ice chips during fluorouracil in this regimen. Use prescribed anti-sickness medicines, pace activities and ask for nutritional, emotional or practical support.

items.title: Pregnancy and fertility
items.text: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. Ask for the contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine; the whole regimen may require longer precautions than one medicine alone.

chapters.title: Visits and treatment sequence
chapters.intro: Know which steps happen in the clinic and at home.

items.title: The exact delivery plan
items.text: Cetuximab on Day 1. Day 1: oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump; planned disconnection around Day 3. A repeating 14-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan.

items.title: Radiotherapy relationship
items.text: This NCCP regimen does not contain a routine radiotherapy course. If radiation is recommended separately, ask whether it is before, during or after these medicines.

items.title: Symptoms and monitoring
items.text: Continue the cetuximab skin plan and mineral checks for two months after the last dose. Persistent numbness after oxaliplatin needs follow-up. Ask which medicines to continue, when to seek help and how response will be assessed.

items.title: Next decisions
items.text: The team reviews benefit, side effects and your priorities. Supportive and palliative care can help alongside active treatment. Ask for a clear next-step and contact plan.

chapters.title: Pauses, recovery and follow-up
chapters.intro: Your team may pause or change one or more medicines. Do not restart or change doses yourself.

items.title: Decisions before restarting
items.text: The team checks the severity and recovery of side effects, previous episodes and the doses you actually received. A standard table dose does not automatically override a prior individual reduction.

items.title: Keep testing appointments
items.text: Blood tests may continue during a treatment pause. Keep monthly electrolyte, magnesium and calcium checks for two months after the last cetuximab dose. Scans and tumour-marker timing follow the consultant plan; these documents do not impose a universal scan interval.

items.title: The interval before chemotherapy
items.text: Cetuximab is given before chemotherapy. Product information requires at least one hour between the end of cetuximab and the start of chemotherapy. Your appointment includes preparation, premedication and observation as well as time connected to a drip.

items.title: Check every medicine and supplement
items.text: Show the team all prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines before treatment and before starting anything new. Certain antiviral medicines, including brivudine and sorivudine, must not be combined with fluorouracil. Tell the team if you take warfarin or phenytoin; extra monitoring may be needed. Do not stop or change medicines yourself.

purpose: The aim is to control advanced bowel cancer and symptoms. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable; your team reviews the plan with you.
schedule_summary: Cetuximab and modified FOLFOX6 start on Day 1, followed by one 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable. No weekly Day 8 cetuximab is scheduled.

day_groups.action: Know the contact number and the next planned visit.

day_groups.body: Keep the arranged professional pump-disconnection appointment. Do not adjust, reconnect or remove it yourself.

support.title: Skin, nails and minerals
support.text: Start the prescribed skin-care plan early, use moisturiser and sun protection, and report painful or infected skin or nails. Keep mineral blood-test appointments during treatment and for two months after cetuximab.

support.title: Bowel symptoms and fluids
support.text: Follow your written rescue plan. Fever, blood, severe pain, reduced urine or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

support.title: Line and pump plan
support.text: Confirm port/PICC preparation, pump connection, home care and professional disconnection around Day 3.

support.title: Comfort and daily life
support.text: Avoid cold drinks and cold exposure as instructed after oxaliplatin; do not suck ice chips during fluorouracil in this regimen. Use prescribed anti-sickness medicines, pace activities and ask for nutritional, emotional or practical support.

support.title: The whole treatment plan
support.text: Ask how and when the team will assess benefit, which blood tests continue during a pause, and what happens after the final dose. Mineral checks continue monthly for two months after the last antibody treatment.

support.title: Nerves and cold exposure
support.text: Tell the team about numbness, tingling, cold-triggered throat symptoms or difficulty with buttons or walking before the next dose. Avoid cold exposure as instructed; do not use ice chips during fluorouracil in this oxaliplatin regimen. Breathing difficulty always needs urgent assessment.

support.title: Recovery and the next dose
support.text: A delay or reduction is individual. Tell the team about ongoing side effects and previous dose changes; do not assume a calendar date or a stamped card means that treatment can restart.

evidence.title: OPUS: exploratory extended RAS analysis
evidence.intro: Studies can help explain why a treatment is offered. The schedule, previous medicines and tumour tests affect how well the evidence fits you.
evidence.population: Metastatic colorectal cancer with validated extended RAS-wild-type status. The NCCP document retains older KRAS wording; the current Erbitux SmPC requires extended RAS testing.
evidence.interpretation: Adding cetuximab to FOLFOX4 improved tumour shrinkage in a small selected trial group. That analysis did not establish a clear survival advantage. Tumour shrinkage is not the same as cure. The trial used weekly cetuximab and FOLFOX4, so its results are indirect for this fortnightly modified FOLFOX6 plan.

chronology_notes.title: Your planned visits
chronology_notes.text: Cetuximab on Day 1. Day 1: oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump; planned disconnection around Day 3. A repeating 14-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan.

chronology_notes.title: No guaranteed safe days
chronology_notes.text: An infection, reaction or other urgent problem can occur at any time. The graph does not predict a personal low point.

chronology_notes.title: Care continues
chronology_notes.text: Continue the skin-care plan and mineral checks arranged after cetuximab. Numbness or tingling can persist after oxaliplatin; tell your team if it affects daily tasks. Ask which medicines to continue and when your next review is planned.

logistics.title: Visits, access and care between treatments
logistics.intro: Cetuximab and modified FOLFOX6 start on Day 1, followed by one 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable. No weekly Day 8 cetuximab is scheduled.

steps.title: Before the first visit
steps.text: Confirm the exact regimen, tests, medicines, emergency number and treatment goal. Discuss which central line is suitable and arrange pump training.

steps.title: At the treatment unit
steps.text: Fortnightly cetuximab infusion time is set from the dose and safe infusion rate; the first dose may take longer. Oxaliplatin and folinic acid are usually infused over about two hours, before fluorouracil. Blood review, preparation, premedicines and observation add time; infusion time is not the total appointment length.

steps.title: After the infusion
steps.text: The fluorouracil pump runs for about 46 hours. Confirm where and when it will be disconnected, usually around Day 3; do not disconnect it yourself unless specifically trained.

steps.title: Between doses
steps.text: Use the written symptom and support plan; do not wait for the next appointment if urgent symptoms appear.

steps.title: The next decision
steps.text: Confirm the next visit after any delay or dose change. Treatment continues only while the oncology team judges benefit and tolerability acceptable. Follow-up mineral checks continue after the final EGFR-antibody dose where applicable.

details.title: Transport and daily life
details.text: Plan transport if antihistamines, symptoms or other medicines affect driving. Ask for practical, work, nutrition or emotional support.

details.title: If treatment changes
details.text: Ask which component has been held and which visits remain. A treatment delay does not automatically cancel blood tests, line care or symptom follow-up.

administration_text: Fortnightly cetuximab infusion time is set from the dose and safe infusion rate; the first dose may take longer. Oxaliplatin and folinic acid are usually infused over about two hours, before fluorouracil. Blood review, preparation, premedicines and observation add time; infusion time is not the total appointment length. The fluorouracil pump runs for about 46 hours. Confirm where and when it will be disconnected, usually around Day 3; do not disconnect it yourself unless specifically trained. Cetuximab premedication includes an antihistamine and corticosteroid at least one hour before treatment. The first two infusions have a one-hour post-infusion observation; the team may change observation after two tolerated doses. The EMA product information specifies that chemotherapy starts at least one hour after cetuximab ends; the team includes this interval in your appointment.

patient_summary.purpose: To control advanced bowel cancer and symptoms. Your team reviews benefit, side effects and the ongoing plan.
patient_summary.schedule: Cetuximab and modified FOLFOX6 on Day 1 every 14 days; a 46-hour fluorouracil pump ends around Day 3. No Day 8 infusion.

phases.title: A repeating 14-day cycle
phases.text: Modified FOLFOX6 includes oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil.

preparation: Bring your medicine list; confirm tests, the skin-care plan and working urgent contact numbers.
Confirm your pump-care instructions, professional disconnection and written symptom rescue plan.

monitoring.when: Confirm RAS result, blood count, kidney/liver tests; DPD before fluorouracil unless already tested.
Blood count, kidney/liver tests before each cycle; weekly counts if delayed for low counts. Review skin, bowel and nerve symptoms.
Monitor during treatment; monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last antibody dose.
ECG if cardiac function is compromised; formal neuropathy review every two cycles.
Scans and markers follow the consultant plan. Follow unresolved effects.

cycle_expectations: Report cold sensitivity or persistent tingling; avoid cold exposure as instructed.
Fever, sudden illness, severe diarrhoea, poor intake or reduced urine needs urgent advice. There are no guaranteed safe days.
